summary: Configured persistent RADIUS authentication from node2 to node1 on RHEL 9.8. Correct credentials receive Access-Accept, incorrect credentials receive Access-Reject, and an invalid client secret receives no accepted response. Both nodes passed sequential reboot and recovery verification.
actions_performed: Installed RHEL-supported FreeRADIUS 3.0.27 software without changing the OS release or kernel.
Configured node2 as a dedicated RADIUS client with a generated secret stored using restrictive permissions.
Loaded the demonstration account from access.txt without modifying the handover files.
Enabled radiusd, opened UDP/1812, and validated the server configuration.
Tested all required authentication outcomes before and after rebooting both nodes sequentially.

evidence.requirement: Dedicated RADIUS client and demonstration user
evidence.summary: node2 has a root-only client secret; node1 has the dedicated node2 client, protected server-side secret, demonstration-user record, valid configuration, and active UDP/1812 listener.
Tests before and after both reboots prove Access-Accept for correct credentials, Access-Reject for a wrong password, and no accepted response with the wrong client secret.

evidence.requirement: Installed OS release and kernel retained
evidence.summary: Both nodes remained on RHEL 9.8 with kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8.x86_64.
access.txt and client-notes.txt retain their original SHA-256 hashes on both nodes after configuration and restarts.
Captured the healthy baseline, acknowledged safe reboot, changed boot ID, restored radiusd/listener/firewall/configuration/data, and successful post-restart authentication.
Captured the healthy baseline, acknowledged safe reboot, changed boot ID, preserved client configuration and handover data, and all required post-restart authentication outcomes.
